records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Betsiamites is directly mapped on the downstream trunk and northern approach. Rivière aux Sables is directly mapped on the southern Itomamo–Pipmuacan approach chosen by the model as its mainstem. Reservoir and lake names retain their own scopes; neither the model role nor common drainage membership makes the entire southwestern route Rivière Betsiamites.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The southern north-flowing feeder, Itomamo passage, west-to-east Pipmuacan crossing, southeast Betsiamites descent and separate northern Manouanis approach jointly distinguish this selection from the neighboring Shipshaw, Portneuf, Sault aux Cochons and Outardes systems. The selected mainstem is not replaced by the separately selected northern named Betsiamites source corridor.
records.region: Québec, Canada: Mont-Valin and the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean/Côte-Nord lake country, Réservoir Pipmuacan, and the lower Betsiamites toward the Saint-Laurent west of Pessamit.
records.completion_scope: Completed for representative-system identity and regional correspondence of all five selected fragments. The earliest southern small feeder, precise headwater naming transitions, reservoir shore crossings and exact estuarine endpoint remain unassigned; these limits do not leave the supported system identity access-pending.

naming_scope_details.route_qualifier: aux Sables–Itomamo–Pipmuacan is an editorial description of the selected southwestern approach, not an official compound hydronym.
naming_scope_details.southern_headwater_scope: The southwest feeder is located in the mapped Doumic–Moncouche–Le Marié lake country. These are regional passage anchors, not a claim that every modeled vertex occupies a named lake. The initial minor feeder remains unnamed in this finding.
naming_scope_details.mainstem_scope: Southern feeder to the aux Sables/Itomamo route, then Pipmuacan and the lower Betsiamites. A downstream representative label must not erase the separately named southern watercourse or waterbodies.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: The two northern modeled tributary fragments represent the upper Betsiamites/Manouanis-to-Pipmuacan corridor. Model mainstem/tributary roles are not official hydronym hierarchy. La Tourette, Praslin, Portneuf, Sault aux Cochons and Outardes context does not make those unselected branches part of this selected route.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: Pipmuacan and the downstream Bersimis impoundment/development setting are separately identified. The sources support regional continuity only; no claim is made that a modeled line resolves contemporary diversion, operational water routing or engineering structures.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Betsiamites estuarine approach toward the Saint-Laurent; exact mouth and tidal limits not assigned.
naming_scope_details.historical_source_scope: BAPE report 145 has legal deposit 2001 and describes proposed diversions and then-current conditions. MRNF maps have legal deposit 2012 and a 2011 topographic base; CEHQ maps are 2011, with the 07/13 sheet updated in 2014. Historical project, legal, operating and flow statements are not adopted as current facts.
naming_scope_details.name_limits: Bersimis is used only where the acquired maps name developments/reservoirs. No full river-alias equivalence, Indigenous-name equivalence, formal naming date or Korean form is established. Incidental gazetteer and encyclopedia search excerpts are excluded.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Fragment boundaries are not naming boundaries. Modeled length is not an official river length. Regional map correspondence does not establish surveyed shoreline or exact first/last waterbody identity.

records.supported_name_scope: Río San Juan is supported as the representative receiving-system name. The modeled upper mainstem follows Río Tatamá before entering San Juan; the selected eastern tributary systems and Calima retain separate identities. The terminal route follows the southern Brazo San Juan / Boca San Juan approach, rather than the northern Cabeceras–Docordó branch. This does not assign San Juan as one scalar name to every selected piece.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The Pacific San Juan system reached by the Tatamá tributary near Santa Cecilia, continuing through Tadó and Istmina to its southern delta approach. Distinguished from the Atrato to the north, Baudó and separate coastal rivers to the west, Cauca east of the divide, and the separate northern delta outlets.
records.region: Pacific-draining western Colombia: Risaralda, Chocó and the northern Valle del Cauca margin.
records.completion_scope: All four mainstem and fifteen tributary stage fragments were reviewed as one generalized selection. Detailed upper cartography and regional drainage/basin maps establish the receiving system and connections; municipal and official geographical prose distinguish the selected southern delta route. Individual minor feeder names and exact tributary name transitions remain unassigned where the sources do not justify them. These local naming limits do not leave a material uncertainty about the representative San Juan system.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not an official measurement of the natural San Juan river.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Separate Tatamá tributary route followed by the San Juan receiving trunk; no equation of the modeled source with the official San Juan source.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Ingará/Surama/Tamaná, Cajón, Sipí/Garrapatas, Copomá/Cucurrupí and Calima contexts remain separate from the representative San Juan name. Where only membership and connection are supported, component names remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Southern Brazo San Juan to Boca San Juan coastal approach near El Choncho; other delta branches and precise shoreline positions are not selected-name claims.
naming_scope_details.remaining_work: No further source acquisition is needed for the bounded representative-system finding. Scalar, accepted, Korean and automatic assignments remain disabled.

records.supported_name_scope: The selection combines a short unnamed feeder into Kigalik River, the lower Kigalik, a substantial Ikpikpuk River reach, a modeled eastward lake-plain connection, a Teshekpuk Lake crossing, and the northeastern Garry Creek/lake corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The western approach enters Kigalik River, not Titaluk River or the eastern Maybe Creek headwater. The route later leaves the Ikpikpuk corridor eastward, south of the prominently mapped western Teshekpuk connection. It crosses the Teshekpuk Lake setting and turns north through the Garry Creek/lake corridor toward Pogik Bay; it does not continue along the Ikpikpuk delta to Smith Bay, the western Chipp branch, or the Kogru River route into Harrison Bay. Its northeastern endpoint remains inland in the lake-rich corridor rather than at a verified coastal river mouth.
records.region: North Slope, National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, United States
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic correspondence and naming-scope assessment of the whole selected fragment. Readable original agency maps cover the unnamed feeder, lower Kigalik, middle Ikpikpuk, Teshekpuk setting, and northeastern lake/creek corridor. The hold is caused by a composite route, generalized connections that are not established named natural channels, an interior-lake crossing, and an inland terminal lake setting. It is not a substantial missing-map gap. Follow-up is required before reach subdivision, whole-group naming or application; continuous natural flow through the model route is not established.

naming_scope_details.whole_group_scope: A single mainstem-role model fragment combines distinct named rivers, an unnamed feeder, lake-plain connectors, a major lake crossing and a northeastern creek/lake corridor. Its single fragment and stage do not establish a single hydronym.
naming_scope_details.headwater_scope: An unnamed northward tributary approach feeds a selected lower Kigalik reach. The actual route is not the full Kigalik source-to-mouth course and not the Maybe Creek or Titaluk headwater alternative.
naming_scope_details.ikpikpuk_scope: Ikpikpuk is supported after the Kigalik–Maybe confluence and through the long middle corridor. The selected eastern departure prevents extending that name over the full group or claiming a selected Smith Bay delta mouth.
naming_scope_details.western_lake_connection_scope: Miguakiak is a mapped nearby river/lake-connection label, not a verified label for the modeled eastward connection south of the conspicuous mapped route. Mayoriak River, shown separately farther north, is also not substituted for this model segment. Current flow direction and seasonal reversals are not determined from these maps.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Teshekpuk Lake is a distinct mapped waterbody. The straight modeled crossing carries no independent natural-channel name, and map proximity alone does not establish that the lake drains east along the selected route.
naming_scope_details.garry_scope: Garry Creek supports the northeastern corridor, with interspersed separately depicted lakes and generalized links. The inland endpoint is not the creek’s official coastal mouth.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: No tributary-role fragments are selected. Maybe Creek, Titaluk River, Oumalik River, Price River and other neighboring waterways are retained as separate geographic context. The western Chipp/delta route, Smith River and Kogru River are not selected substitutes.
naming_scope_details.historical_and_flow_scope: Agency map and report dates bound the evidence. No present perennial connection, flood-stage condition, flow direction, exact shoreline, lake drainage change, surveyed thalweg or current navigability is asserted.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 352.160 km rendered length is a model length, not an official river length. Generalized raster-routing lines and fragment roles cannot define formal naming boundaries. No Korean form, formal naming act or whole-group scalar is established.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic correspondence and naming-scope assessment of the whole selected fragment. Readable original agency maps cover the unnamed feeder, lower Kigalik, middle Ikpikpuk, Teshekpuk setting, and northeastern lake/creek corridor. The hold is caused by a composite route, generalized connections that are not established named natural channels, an interior-lake crossing, and an inland terminal lake setting. It is not a substantial missing-map gap. Follow-up is required before reach subdivision, whole-group naming or application; continuous natural flow through the model route is not established.

records.supported_name_scope: Rio Munim is the representative receiving river. Rio Preto is a separately supported upper component along the selected eastern approach and its broad westward, northward and southwestward bend sequence. No name is forced onto every small initial feeder or every river-to-estuary segment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The model selects the eastern Preto tributary approach, not the more southerly Munim headwaters through the Afonso Cunha/Chapadinha corridor or the separate Iguará approach. Lower Itapecuru is farther west and Parnaíba farther east.
records.region: Northeastern Maranhão, Brazil; Buriti-side Preto approach through the São Benedito do Rio Preto corridor, then lower Munim toward Axixá and the São José bay approach.
records.completion_scope: Both selected mainstem-role pieces were considered together. Readable regional maps cover the eastern beginning, full Preto approach and bend sequence, receiving Munim junction and northward lower ending. Explicit hydrographic prose and the São Benedito station corroborate the component naming. This is a regional correspondence assessment, not a surveyed river source, naming-transition vertex or current shoreline determination.

naming_scope_details.representative_name: Rio Munim, qualified by northeastern Maranhão.
naming_scope_details.selected_upper_component: Rio Preto approach from the western Buriti setting through the northern side of Anapurus/Mata Roma/Chapadinha and the São Benedito do Rio Preto corridor. The smallest initial segment and exact source/name transition remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.excluded_upper_routes: Southern upper Munim and Iguará remain separate tributary/headwater approaches. Their official river names and station locations are not substituted for the chosen eastern route.
naming_scope_details.tributary_role_scope: Two selected pieces have model mainstem roles and no separate tributary-role piece is present. Nevertheless the natural Preto is a tributary component, demonstrating that the model role is not a hydronym assignment.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Munim near the São José bay approach beyond Axixá; not the complete bay, western Itapecuru outlet or open ocean.
naming_scope_details.source_scope: Historical cartographic editions and the 2026 SEMA station table support geographic identity. No present discharge, perennial continuity, legal boundary, reservoir operation, water-quality condition or current station operation is asserted.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 351.353 km model length is not an official length of either Munim or Preto. Stage and fragment boundaries do not set natural naming limits. No Korean name is invented.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
